squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says a December hike would be prudent if the data hold, and sees inflation slightly above 4% at year-end
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said inflation is likely to end the year a little above 4%, with more to come before the peak, and he expects core and food inflation to pick up. He also said oil prices could move a lot before the December meeting, that he would like markets to reprice in line with the wider macro picture, that Europe's resilience is reassuring, and that France's fiscal problems need to be fixed in Paris.

squawks.headline: Russia, Ukraine and US trilateral talks reportedly begin in Abu Dhabi
squawks.detail: Reports say three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US have started in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine's Umerov said the delegation's first meeting is with European, NATO and EU representatives and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner.

squawks.headline: Canada's foreign minister hopes for progress on US tariffs after the midterm elections
squawks.detail: Canada's foreign minister said she hopes for progress on US tariffs once the US midterm elections are over. No timetable or specific measures were reported.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures drop 2% to $90.66 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures were reported down 2% at $90.66 a barrel in early European trading on 10 November.

squawks.headline: Ukraine peace talks get under way in Abu Dhabi, with US, Ukrainian and European delegations meeting
squawks.detail: Market commentary accounts report that talks have begun in Abu Dhabi and that the US delegation is meeting Ukrainian and European delegations. No market reaction is reported.

squawks.headline: Norway's October underlying CPI slows to 2.7% y/y, matching forecasts and down from 3.0%
squawks.detail: Norway's underlying inflation rose 0.3% m/m in October, against a forecast of 0.4% and 0.2% the previous month. Headline CPI was 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% estimate.

squawks.headline: Norway's October CPI rises 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% forecast and up from 3.4%
squawks.detail: Norwegian consumer prices rose 0.3% on the month, after 0.5% the previous month. The annual rate of 3.6% came in a little below the 3.7% forecast and above the previous 3.4%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin expects ECB policy continuity if Knot or de Cos becomes president
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said he expects continuity at the central bank if either Knot or de Cos takes over.

squawks.headline: ADNOC CFO says LNG exports through Hormuz are still below pre-conflict levels despite month-on-month improvement
squawks.detail: ADNOC's chief financial officer said LNG cargoes leaving the Strait of Hormuz are improving each month but have not yet returned to pre-conflict levels. He added that the company has made no decisions on alternative LNG export facilities.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says there are positive signs on energy prices
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said on 10 November that the central bank sees positive signs on energy prices.

squawks.headline: France says Europeans will attend Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks, rules out European security talks with Russia before a ceasefire
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister said European representatives will take part in the Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi. France also said there will be no discussions with Russia on European security until a ceasefire is in place and peace in Ukraine is secured.

squawks.headline: US crude futures fall 2% to $85.11 a barrel
squawks.detail: US oil futures were reported down 2% at $85.11 a barrel in early trading on 10 November.

squawks.headline: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli does not rule out a December rate hike but says she needs more information
squawks.detail: Lombardelli says she would not exclude a December rate rise but does not yet have enough information, according to The Guardian. She also says hiring in the UK labour market has fallen off sharply without much sign of redundancies, and that young people are being hurt by a low-gear economy.

squawks.headline: Thames Water creditors ready a 'final' offer as PM Burnham weighs whether to nationalise the company, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Thames Water's creditors are preparing what they describe as a final offer. It says the prime minister has been reluctant to take the company into state ownership despite having supported the idea earlier.

squawks.headline: Laden LNG tanker exits from the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest monthly level in October since the Iran war began
squawks.detail: Reuters cites vessel tracking data showing the monthly count of laden LNG tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since the US-Iran conflict disrupted shipping.

squawks.headline: US military moves aircraft out of a second UK base after an Iranian threat, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US military evacuated aircraft from a UK airbase on Monday following a threat from Iran.

squawks.headline: China's October crude imports reach their highest since March but are down 13.3% y/y
squawks.detail: Official Chinese data show October crude oil imports fell 13.3% from a year earlier but were the highest since March, after the war on Iran disrupted Middle East supplies.

squawks.headline: Japan's 30-year JGB auction tail widens to 0.35 from 0.16; 30-year yield rises 2.5bp to 3.865% afterwards
squawks.detail: The tail at Japan's 30-year government bond sale widened to 0.35, from 0.16 at the previous auction. The 30-year JGB yield rose 2.5bp to 3.865% after the result.

squawks.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1tn in the first 10 months of the year
squawks.detail: The FT and Reuters report China's January to October trade surplus passed $1tn, led by exports of high-tech goods linked to AI infrastructure. Customs data put October exports up 28.7% y/y in yuan terms and imports up 34.7%.

squawks.headline: China's October dollar exports rise 35.2% y/y, above the 33.5% forecast; trade surplus of $105.28bn falls short of $125.8bn poll
squawks.detail: Chinese customs data show October dollar-denominated exports up 35.2% y/y against a poll of 33.5%, with the trade surplus at $105.28bn against a forecast of $125.8bn. The surplus with the United States was $32.71bn, and yuan-denominated exports rose 28.7% y/y.

squawks.headline: Japan offers 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year government bonds with a 4.200% coupon
squawks.detail: Japan's government is offering 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year JGBs carrying a 4.200% coupon. Separately, Finance Minister Katayama said no decision has been taken on tax incentives for retail JGBs and left the debate to the LDP.

squawks.headline: Barclays data show UK consumer spending up 2.3% y/y in October, the most since July 2025, while confidence hits its lowest since April
squawks.detail: Barclays said UK card spending rose 2.3% year on year in October, up from 2.0% in September and the largest increase since July 2025. It also said consumer confidence in October was the weakest since April.

squawks.headline: UK BRC retail sales rise 1.1% y/y, a little below the 1.2% forecast
squawks.detail: The British Retail Consortium's retail sales monitor shows annual growth of 1.1%, against a forecast of 1.2% and up from 1.0% previously.

squawks.headline: BoJ October summary of opinions shows several members favour further rate rises towards neutral
squawks.detail: In the Bank of Japan's October summary of opinions, one member said underlying inflation has reached 2% and the policy rate must reach neutral soon, and one said Japan's neutral rate is likely well above 1%. Other members urged caution, citing some economic weakness and the need to watch financial conditions for several months after each rate rise.

squawks.headline: Japan's September household spending falls 6.8% y/y, a much steeper drop than the 3.1% expected
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show household spending down 6.8% year on year and down 2.8% month on month in September, against a poll forecast of a 0.3% monthly rise.

squawks.headline: Trump tells reporters US military action against Iran does not look necessary for now
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that US military action against Iran did not currently appear necessary, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Iran's top security official denies talks with the US are taking place and tells Washington to accept Tehran's seven conditions
squawks.detail: Iran's top security official told the US to stop putting out false reports of talks that he said do not exist. He also said it was time for Washington to give in to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US has another aircraft carrier ready as Iran talks continue
squawks.detail: US President Trump said in remarks on Iran on Monday evening that the US has a further aircraft carrier loaded up. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Qatar's prime minister says he met Trump and Vance to discuss ways to move Iran negotiations forward
squawks.detail: Qatar's prime minister said the meeting with US President Trump and Vice President Vance covered ways to make progress in negotiations with Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran is effectively finished as a military force and the US is keeping Iran at the status quo
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Monday evening, and repeated that he sees momentum towards ending the conflict. The posts in this batch report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy disables navigation systems of four large oil tankers using an unauthorised Strait of Hormuz route, Press TV says
squawks.detail: Iranian state broadcaster Press TV reports that the Revolutionary Guard navy disabled the navigation systems of four large oil tankers over the past 24 hours, leaving them unable to continue through the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says he sees positive momentum towards ending the Iran conflict and that an Iranian nuclear weapon is non-negotiable
squawks.detail: In a Truth Social post, US President Trump said all parties agree that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. He added that the US stands ready to act if the situation in the Middle East changes, but that this now looks quite unlikely.

squawks.headline: Trump says he had an excellent conversation with Qatar's prime minister
squawks.detail: The US president said this in a Truth Social post. Earlier reports said the talks covered efforts towards a deal with Iran.

squawks.headline: Canada extends tariff relief on goods hit by US tariffs by one year, to 30 June 2028
squawks.detail: Canada's finance minister said the general remission for US tariffs is extended to 30 June 2028. Relief will also cover non-steel goods used in mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction, and certain imported goods that are in short supply in Canada.

squawks.headline: Arab and Muslim leaders press Trump not to restart war with Iran, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Arab and Muslim leaders are trying to ease tensions, amid fears that the US president will resume hostilities with Iran.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine's gains on the battlefield give Kyiv a stronger hand in peace talks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said recent battlefield successes have strengthened Kyiv's negotiating position. The remarks come ahead of this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Trump says this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine offer a chance of a possible breakthrough
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Abu Dhabi talks on the war in Ukraine, due this week, could bring a breakthrough. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says US is prepared to strike Iran if needed, though Qatar and Saudi Arabia favour a peaceful settlement
squawks.detail: Speaking to Reuters after talks with Qatar's leader, US President Trump said Qatar would prefer a peaceful outcome with Iran but the US stands ready to carry out strikes if necessary. He added that Saudi Arabia would also prefer a peaceful solution to the conflict.

squawks.headline: Trump's talks with Qatar's prime minister on Iran deal efforts were positive, a diplomat tells Axios
squawks.detail: Axios cites a diplomat who described the talks between President Trump and Qatar's prime minister as positive. Qatar is helping to mediate between the US and Iran on the details of a deal.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle at $92.57 a barrel, down $5.75 or 5.85% on the day
squawks.detail: Brent futures closed at $92.57 a barrel, $5.75 or 5.85% lower on the session.

squawks.headline: Proposed US-Iran framework would reopen Strait of Hormuz, lift naval blockade and free $6bn-$9bn of Iranian assets, Al Arabiya says
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya sources say the Strait of Hormuz would be opened and the naval blockade lifted immediately under the proposed framework, and the US would release $6 billion to $9 billion of Iranian assets if a deal is reached. The sources also say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without setting out the scope of their work.

squawks.headline: US lets Iran enrich uranium at home to 3.67% and Tehran agrees, Al Arabiya sources say; preliminary enrichment deal seen as likely
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, reports that Washington has allowed Iran to enrich uranium domestically to 3.67%, that Tehran has accepted, and that a preliminary agreement on cutting Iran's enrichment is likely. The same sources say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without saying what their duties would cover.

squawks.headline: WTI crude December futures settle at $86.85, down $3.98 or 4.38% on the day
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December crude futures settled at $86.85 a barrel, a fall of $3.98 or 4.38%. NYMEX natural gas December futures settled at $3.2180/MMBtu.

squawks.headline: Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz after using unauthorised routes
squawks.detail: Iran said three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and footage showed one tanker on fire on the shipping route. The posts report that attacks on commercial shipping are continuing; no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: OPEC oil output rises in October to 90% of its pre-war level, Reuters survey finds
squawks.detail: A Reuters survey shows OPEC production rose in October, led by gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq. Exports remain constrained by the Iran war and a US blockade on Iranian shipments.

squawks.headline: Bank of France expects moderate growth in the French economy in the fourth quarter
squawks.detail: The Bank of France says French economic growth will be moderate in the fourth quarter. It had earlier said it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth.

squawks.headline: Bank of France says it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth
squawks.detail: The Bank of France said there is great uncertainty around its assessment of growth. No figures were reported with the comment.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin calls last jobs report healthy but says firms are still in a low-hire, low-fire mode
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin also said ballot measures approved in recent US elections should not stop data centre expansion because firms will find other places to build. He added that it would help if each Fed policy meeting came with two full months of economic data.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy tells European partners he expects sustained Russian attacks on Dnipro bridges aimed at splitting Ukraine
squawks.detail: The FT reports that Ukraine's president has warned European partners he expects Russia to launch sustained attacks on bridges across the Dnipro river in an attempt to cut the country in half. The warning comes during the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says he has no base case for December and sees policy rate around or slightly below neutral
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he has no base case for the December meeting and called the last jobs report healthy, though firms remain in a low-hire, low-fire pattern. He also said it is hard to know how the elections will affect the economy.

squawks.headline: US officials say they do not expect the Abu Dhabi talks to end the Ukraine war, only to clarify each side's positions
squawks.detail: US officials told CBS the Abu Dhabi talks aim to get Russia and Ukraine to set out their positions so compromises can be explored later. They also said Washington wants Russia to agree to multilateral negotiations that include Europe.

squawks.headline: Italian cabinet approves a gas price cap to bring down energy bills
squawks.detail: Italy's cabinet has backed a cap on gas prices intended to lower household and business energy bills, according to a market news report.

squawks.headline: US $58bn 3-year note auction prices at 4.627% with a 0.5bp tail; bid-to-cover falls to 2.53
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $58bn of 3-year notes at a high yield of 4.627%, against 4.932% at the previous auction, with bid-to-cover of 2.53 compared with 2.62 last time. Indirect bidders took 55.48%, directs 35.04% and primary dealers 9.48%, and 73.41% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

squawks.headline: US 3-year when-issued yield stands at 4.622% ahead of $58bn Treasury auction
squawks.detail: The when-issued 3-year US Treasury yield was 4.622% just before the US Treasury's $58 billion 3-year note auction on Monday.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says government debt, rather than consumer debt, is at a historically high level
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said in remarks on Monday that government debt, not consumer debt, is at historic levels.

squawks.headline: US official says Washington seeks NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine and a stronger NATO-Russia Council
squawks.detail: A US official speaking about the Ukraine talks said US security guarantees will be discussed and that Russia is showing positive signs on ending the war. The official also said the US wants to make a NATO-Russia Council more robust.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin calls the US economy remarkably stable, with muted layoffs but bleak consumer sentiment
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said businesses are doing well, with strong earnings, few layoffs and healthy loan pipelines, and that loan demand goes well beyond AI. He said consumer sentiment is bleak but people are still spending because the job market is resilient.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says policymakers can no longer afford to assume supply shocks will fade
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remark in a speech on Monday evening. He said it can no longer be taken for granted that supply shocks will pass on their own.

squawks.headline: US official says Ukraine territorial issues will wait until post-war security architecture is settled; US to press Russia on wider format
squawks.detail: A US official briefing on the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks said the US will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format with Europe at the table after the trilateral meeting, and that both parties are coming with good intentions. The official said territorial questions will not be resolved until the post-war security architecture is known.

squawks.headline: US official says European partners will join the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks and both sides show some private flexibility on territory
squawks.detail: A US official said European partners will take part in the Abu Dhabi talks and that Washington will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format, with daily contact with both Ukraine and Russia. The official also said Kyiv and Moscow have privately shown a little flexibility on territorial concessions, and that NATO will remain central to European collective defence.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says UK activity is more resilient than expected, helped by AI investment, but warns an AI asset bubble threatens stability
squawks.detail: In a speech, Bank of England Governor Bailey said there are growing signs of an early positive supply shock from AI and investment, notably in business services. He also said an AI asset price bubble poses clear financial stability risks, as markets could overvalue AI returns, and that frontier AI has raised cyberattack risks.

squawks.headline: NY Fed survey shows Americans growing more worried about the US labour market outlook
squawks.detail: The New York Fed's consumer expectations survey for October, published on Monday, found US households more concerned about future unemployment. No figures for the labour market measures were given in the report.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin reports broad-based cost pressures, with firms planning to pass higher costs on to customers
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said resilient demand and wide-ranging cost increases are pushing prices up, and that businesses are reporting strong earnings while bankers describe healthy loan pipelines. He said layoffs remain muted and consumers keep spending on the back of a resilient job market, even though consumer sentiment is weak.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says inflation is where the risk lies and policy should move with care despite a clear direction
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the risk sits on the inflation side of the Fed's mandate. He described the US economy as remarkably stable and said the direction of policy is straightforward but changes should be made with care.

squawks.headline: Brent crude falls to a 10-week low after Trump says US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Brent extended last week's losses, which came after the Republicans' midterm defeat, to reach its lowest level in 10 weeks.

squawks.headline: US Treasury sells $95bn of 3-month bills at 4.06% and $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.145%
squawks.detail: The 3-month bill auction had a bid-to-cover of 2.67, down from 2.880, with 79.03% awarded at the high, compared with 4.040% at the previous sale. The 6-month bill drew a bid-to-cover of 2.92, up from 2.890, with 70.91% awarded at the high; its yield compares with 4.150% previously.

squawks.headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve falls to 279.5mn barrels, its lowest level since 1982
squawks.detail: Crude oil held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 279.5mn barrels last week, the lowest since 1982. The report gave no price reaction.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says she has low expectations for the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks and wants clear concessions from Russia
squawks.detail: The EU foreign policy chief said she does not expect much from the Abu Dhabi talks and that Russia needs to make clear concessions.

squawks.headline: Saudi energy ministry source says the East-West pipeline is still operating after the attack and there are no casualties
squawks.detail: A Saudi energy ministry source said the attack in the Medina region caused a limited fire, which has since been put out, and the pipeline's operations were not affected, according to reports.

squawks.headline: Saudi energy ministry source says the East-West oil pipeline was targeted in the Medina region
squawks.detail: Saudi state media cited an energy ministry source as saying the East-West pipeline was targeted in the Medina region. The report gave no details on damage or on any effect on flows.

squawks.headline: France's foreign minister blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for a cyberattack on fridges and says EU sanctions on Iran will follow
squawks.detail: French Foreign Minister Barrot said Iran's ambassador had been summoned and that there will be consequences for Iran. Earlier, Paris prosecutors said the hacks used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices in Iran, and that they were carried out to serve a foreign power.

squawks.headline: Sterling rises against the dollar, recovering most of Friday's fall as oil prices drop
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the pound gained on Monday as concerns over AI stocks, which had lifted the dollar late last week, eased and oil prices fell.

squawks.headline: NY Fed survey: US one-year inflation expectations edge up to 3.91% in October, three-year steady at 3.3%
squawks.detail: The New York Fed's October Survey of Consumer Expectations put one-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.91%, against a 3.79% forecast and 3.9% previously, with three-year expectations unchanged at 3.3%. Expectations of a rising unemployment rate were the highest since April 2020, and expected gas price rises moderated.

squawks.headline: Rosneft rations petrol sales in Russia after a run of Ukrainian strikes on refineries
squawks.detail: According to the FT, the state-owned Rosneft is limiting petrol sales to 30 litres per car in cities and 50 litres on highways. The move comes after a wave of Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.

squawks.headline: Fuel shortages hit Russian regions again after Ukrainian strikes on at least eight major refineries in two weeks
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that fuel shortages have returned to parts of Russia after Ukraine struck at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks. The report says drivers could again face long queues at filling stations.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio urges the EU to drop preference measures and overregulation aimed at US companies
squawks.detail: The US State Department reported that Secretary of State Rubio called for the EU to end preference measures and overregulation that target US companies. The statement followed his talks with French foreign minister Barrot.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says consumer spending has been the main driver of US growth
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said in remarks on Monday that consumer spending has been the main source of US growth. He also repeated that employment and growth are fairly stable.

squawks.headline: Senior Iranian official says Tehran will not hold talks with the US until Washington acts on its seven conditions
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official told Press TV that Iran's position on negotiations with the US has not changed. The official said there will be no plan for talks unless the US takes practical action on Tehran's seven conditions.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says three in five of the richest fifth of households qualify for the £100 Household Energy Payment
squawks.detail: The think tank says the payment is poorly targeted, and notes that one in six of the poorest families report already being unable to afford to heat their homes.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says services inflation is starting to pick up and data centre activity resembles old-style overheating
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee also said the Fed has to accept it has failed on inflation, and that consumer spending has been the main driver of growth.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says growth and employment are stable but the main problem has been inflation
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said employment and growth look fairly steady, that the main problem has been inflation, and that policymakers have to face up to a failure on inflation.

squawks.headline: Saudi and Omani foreign ministers call for diplomatic efforts to continue to contain the regional crisis
squawks.detail: Reports say the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Oman stressed that diplomatic efforts to contain the regional crisis need to continue.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen backs Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks and says Black Sea freedom of navigation must be preserved and restored
squawks.detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she supports the Ukraine peace talks due to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. She also said again that freedom of navigation in the Black Sea must be preserved and restored.

squawks.headline: US wholesale sales rise 2.8% m/m, above the 1.1% forecast; wholesale inventories revised up to 0.7%
squawks.detail: US wholesale sales grew 2.8% month on month, against a 1.1% forecast and a previous reading of 1.8%. Wholesale inventories were revised to 0.7% m/m, against a 0.6% forecast and a previous reading of 0.6%.

squawks.headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says Russia has been pretending to negotiate and hopes for more US sanctions after the midterms
squawks.detail: Kallas says she sees no good will from Moscow and that Russia has not kept to European security arrangements it agreed in the past. She says she hopes further US sanctions will add pressure on Russia after the US midterm elections, and that the EU should lead on European security in line with its treaties.

squawks.headline: Kremlin's Peskov says rare earth metals are not on the agenda at the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said rare earth metals will not be discussed at this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Brent crude losses deepen to 5% on the day
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that Brent crude's decline has reached 5%. Oil had already been falling after Trump said further US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz threatens to block the EU's next budget unless the bloc unanimously agrees more financial support for Ukraine
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Friedrich Merz is threatening to withhold Germany's agreement on the EU's next budget unless member states unanimously agree additional funding for Kyiv. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Dallas and New York Fed launch a pilot survey of the private credit market
squawks.detail: The Federal Reserve Banks of Dallas and New York said in a statement that they opened a pilot survey of the private credit market on 9 November.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says the Abu Dhabi talks must show whether Russia is really willing to negotiate
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister commented on this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, saying they need to show whether Moscow is serious about negotiating. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield falls to about 4.69%, its lowest since 25 September
squawks.detail: France's 10-year government bond yield fell to around 4.69% on Monday afternoon, its lowest level since 25 September, according to a market wire report.

squawks.headline: WTI crude drops to $86.60, its lowest level since early September
squawks.detail: US crude fell as low as $86.60 a barrel in Monday trade, its lowest since early September, according to market reports.

squawks.headline: USTR pauses action on China's shipbuilding sector until 10 January 2027 and extends 178 China tariff exclusions
squawks.detail: According to a Federal Register notice, the US Trade Representative has suspended any action on China's shipbuilding and maritime sector until 10 January 2027 to allow further talks. It also said it would further extend all 178 current exclusions linked to China's technology transfer, intellectual property and innovation.

squawks.headline: Eurogroup President says a decision on the next ECB president should ideally be made by the end of the year
squawks.detail: The Eurogroup President said the ideal outcome would be to choose a successor to Lagarde as ECB president by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Qatari official says the US and Iran are working through deal details with mediators and calls reports on the proposal's terms false
squawks.detail: An unnamed Qatari official said the US and Iran are in contact with mediators over the details of a deal. The same official rejected circulating reports about the content of the US-Iran proposal as false.

squawks.headline: Trump backs Iraqi PM's proposals to end the Iran war and asks him to pass them on to Tehran
squawks.detail: Reports of a phone call between Trump and Iraq's prime minister say Trump approved the Iraqi proposals for ending the war with Iran. He also asked the prime minister to convey them to Tehran.

squawks.headline: Iraq's prime minister puts forward proposals to end the Iran war in a phone call with Trump, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources report that Iraq's prime minister set out proposals to end the Iran war during a phone call with US President Trump. No details of the proposals were given.

squawks.headline: Iranian official Bagheri says moving enriched material out of Iran is not on the agenda, Iranian reports say
squawks.detail: Iranian media reports cite Bagheri as saying that taking enriched material out of Iran is not under discussion, amid the running US-Iran talks. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Canada announces more sanctions on Russia aimed at reducing its missile capabilities
squawks.detail: The Canadian government announced the additional sanctions against Russia in a statement on Monday. The statement says they are meant to reduce Russia's missile capabilities.

squawks.headline: France extends its €1,000 fuel bonus cap into 2027, finance minister Lescure says
squawks.detail: French finance minister Lescure says the cap of €1,000 on the fuel bonus will continue into 2027. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: Lavrov says security issues are the main topic of the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks, which aim to agree principles for a settlement
squawks.detail: Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov said the Abu Dhabi talks will centre on security issues for Russia, Ukraine and the wider region. He said they aim to agree principles that would be approved when talks on a comprehensive settlement in Ukraine conclude.

squawks.headline: European Commission says the EU must be present in any talks on a European security framework, responding to Kushner's proposal
squawks.detail: Responding to a proposal from Kushner, the European Commission said that deciding any European security framework is a matter for the EU, so the EU needs to take part in such discussions.

squawks.headline: France to lift its minimum wage by 1.6% to €1,502, with the increase brought forward to 1 December
squawks.detail: France's labour minister says the government will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% to €1,502. The minister says the increase will now take effect on 1 December.

squawks.headline: Brent crude falls to an intraday low below $96/bbl
squawks.detail: Brent crude falls below $96 a barrel and hits a new intraday low on Monday. Earlier in the session, prices had already fallen after Trump said further US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely.

squawks.headline: Iran reportedly drops its demand to control the Strait of Hormuz and charge transit fees, Israel Hayom says
squawks.detail: Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reports that Iran appears to have dropped its demand to control the Strait of Hormuz and collect fees from ships passing through. There is no official confirmation from Tehran in the inputs.

squawks.headline: Centre for Cities report looks at Mayor of London's view that new fiscal powers could back more than £10bn of infrastructure borrowing
squawks.detail: The Centre for Cities has published analysis of how London's borrowing plans of more than £10bn would fit within national fiscal rules, and compares them with Madrid. The Mayor of London has said new fiscal powers could support that level of infrastructure borrowing.

squawks.headline: Turkey's Erdogan says he told Trump on a call that Ankara opposes any new wave of attacks on Iran
squawks.detail: Turkish President Erdogan said he raised Turkey's concerns about further strikes on Iran during a call with US President Trump. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia lifts Riyadh alert a day after a Houthi attack damaged an Aramco office building
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence authorities said on Monday that the danger in Riyadh had passed, minutes after raising an alert, Reuters reported. The alert came a day after an attack by Yemen's Houthis damaged an office building belonging to Saudi Aramco in the capital.

squawks.headline: Gulf stock markets rise in early Monday trade after Trump signals new US strikes on Iran are unlikely
squawks.detail: Reuters reports Gulf stock markets gained early on Monday after President Trump indicated that new strikes on Iran were unlikely while talks continue to end the eight-month conflict.

squawks.headline: Eurozone Sentix investor confidence comes in at 2.4, above the 2.05 forecast but down from 2.7
squawks.detail: The Sentix investor confidence index for the eurozone was 2.4 in the latest reading. The forecast was 2.05 and the previous reading was 2.7.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says this week's Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks are a three-way meeting between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the US
squawks.detail: Asked whether European countries could join the talks in Abu Dhabi this week, the Kremlin said the format is Russia and Ukraine with the US as mediator. It added that the US and Ukraine each have their own channels to the Europeans.

squawks.headline: Oil prices fall as Trump says further US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely
squawks.detail: City AM's markets blog reports that oil prices are lower on Monday morning after President Trump said new strikes on Iran were highly unlikely. The FTSE 100 is reported higher at the open.

squawks.headline: Dutch finance minister says the next ECB president should be chosen on merit, not through political bargaining
squawks.detail: The Dutch finance minister said the choice of Lagarde's successor should be based on merit and kept out of political discussions. Spain and the Netherlands both have candidates in the race.

squawks.headline: Iraq prices December Basrah Medium to Asia at a $8.80/b discount and Basrah Heavy at a $11.80/b discount
squawks.detail: Iraq has set its December official selling prices for crude sold to Asia: Basrah Medium at a discount of $8.80 a barrel and Basrah Heavy at a discount of $11.80 a barrel.

squawks.headline: Spain's economy minister says he is optimistic de Cos can win the ECB presidency
squawks.detail: Spain's economy minister said he is optimistic about Spanish candidate de Cos's chances of becoming ECB president. De Cos and the Netherlands' Knot are the two candidates the Eurogroup has named.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says mediators have stopped travelling since the US midterm results
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister said mediators in the US-Iran talks have made no trips since the US midterm election results came out. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: German exports grow 2% m/m in September, beating expectations
squawks.detail: Germany's federal statistics office said on Monday that exports rose 2% on the month in September, more than expected.

squawks.headline: China extends its suspension of export controls aimed at US companies
squawks.detail: A market news feed reported that China will extend its suspension of export controls targeting US companies. The report gave no new expiry date. It follows China's decision to keep its extra tariff on US imports suspended for two more months.

squawks.headline: EU Economy Commissioner Dombrovskis says the economy faces uncertainty and downside risks
squawks.detail: EU Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said on Monday morning that the economy faces uncertainty and downside risks. The reports gave no figures.

squawks.headline: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman says the US Iron Gate task force is meant to divert attention from the US midterm results
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei said the US Task Force Iron Gate operation is a way of deflecting attention from the outcome of the US midterm elections. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's Foreign Ministry calls Tehran's two-day proposal the most reasonable offer in talks with the US
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's two-day proposal is the most reasonable one under discussion. He also said pressure should not damage Iran's ties with Iraq.

squawks.headline: UAE's Gargash says a full US-Iran settlement looks difficult and warns of prolonged regional uncertainty
squawks.detail: Senior Emirati official Anwar Gargash said on Monday that a comprehensive political settlement to end the more than eight-month US-Iran war appeared difficult, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: German trade surplus narrows to 15.6bn, below the 19.4bn forecast, as imports jump 4.2% m/m
squawks.detail: Germany's seasonally adjusted trade balance came in at 15.6bn against a 19.4bn forecast and 19.5bn previously. Imports rose 4.2% month on month, against a 0.5% forecast and 0.9% previously.

squawks.headline: Russian Foreign Ministry says the Russia-US diesel deal could allow business ties between the two countries to recover gradually
squawks.detail: TASS reported the Russian Foreign Ministry's comments on the diesel deal between Russia and the US. The ministry described the deal as an opening for a gradual restoration of business ties.

squawks.headline: Chinese banks sharply raise dollar deposit rates, in some cases above 4%, as Beijing seeks to slow the yuan's rally
squawks.detail: Reuters, citing sources, reports that several Chinese banks have lifted dollar deposit rates in recent weeks, in some cases above US benchmarks. Exporters are reported to be hoarding cash.

squawks.headline: ECB presidency candidate Knot says he would act without hesitation in a debt crisis
squawks.detail: Klaas Knot, one of two candidates to succeed Lagarde, told the FT he would be prepared to create new crisis-fighting tools if needed.

squawks.headline: Iranian official says an overnight US strike hit Qeshm Island but left key infrastructure and services intact
squawks.detail: An Iranian provincial official, quoted by Fars News, said the overnight US strike on Qeshm Island caused no disruption to essential services. Separately, Israel's Kan broadcaster reports that Israeli and US military officials support further military action against Iran.

squawks.headline: Iran says no unauthorised vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz overnight after southern navigation aids were destroyed
squawks.detail: An unnamed Revolutionary Guards Navy official told Iranian state media on Monday that no unauthorised vessels used the route overnight, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Japan's 40-year government bond yield rises to 3.990%
squawks.detail: The 40-year JGB yield climbs to 3.990% in Asian trading on Monday.

squawks.headline: Iranian state TV says navigation aids in southern Hormuz are destroyed, halting transit on an unauthorised route
squawks.detail: Iranian state television, citing an unnamed Revolutionary Guards navy official, says navigation aid systems in the southern Strait of Hormuz were destroyed. It says no vessels used the unauthorised route overnight.

squawks.headline: China keeps its 24% extra tariff on US imports suspended for two more months, holding the 10% rate
squawks.detail: China's finance ministry says the suspension of the additional 24% tariff on US imports is extended for two months, until 10 January, while the 10% tariff stays in place. China's transport ministry separately extends its suspension of special port fees on US vessels, and its shipping and shipbuilding probe, until 10 January 2027.

squawks.headline: China's October PPI rises 5.7% y/y, above the 5.3% forecast, while CPI slows to 0.7% against 0.8% expected
squawks.detail: Chinese producer prices rose 5.7% on the year in October, up from 5.0%, and 0.7% on the month after 1.2%. Consumer prices rose 0.7% y/y after 0.9% and were flat on the month; core CPI was 0.8% against 0.9% forecast and 1.0% previously.

squawks.headline: JGB yields rise across the curve, with 5-year up 6.5bp to 2.110% and 30-year up 4bp to 3.865%
squawks.detail: Japanese government bond yields climbed in Asian trading on Monday: the 5-year rose 6.5bp to 2.110%, the 20-year rose 5bp to 3.595% and the 30-year rose 4bp to 3.865%.

squawks.headline: Trump says he expects the war in Ukraine to end soon and a Ukraine of a different shape afterwards
squawks.detail: The US president made the remarks in a pre-recorded CBS 60 Minutes interview released on Sunday.

squawks.headline: Japan's largest daily intervention in July–September was 7.98 trillion yen on 30 July, Finance Ministry data show
squawks.detail: The Finance Ministry also reported foreign reserves of $1,179.119bn at the end of October, compared with $1,178.396bn at the end of September. Benchmark 10-year JGB futures fell 0.36 point in early trade.

squawks.headline: RBA's Hunter says AI demand will lift inflation in the near term and flags risk of disorderly asset repricing
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Hunter said AI could raise financial stability risks if returns disappoint, although its long-run effect on inflation is likely to be broadly neutral. She said there is limited evidence that AI has significantly boosted productivity or employment in advanced economies.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio calls Iran talks unproductive and says Tehran's demands are unacceptable
squawks.detail: Rubio said the US would pursue a diplomatic solution with Iran where one is possible but that this is not always the case. He described some Iranian demands as outrageous.

squawks.headline: Kurdistan region says nearly 2.8 GW of power lost from the grid after the attack on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field
squawks.detail: The Kurdistan region's electricity ministry gave the figure after production at Khor Mor was halted by a drone attack. Iraqi Kurdish ministries say they are working to limit the impact, and Iraq's armed forces command reports no casualties on initial assessment.

squawks.headline: Trump says Task Force Iron Gate is fully in effect in Iran and, with the naval blockade, very little moves in or out
squawks.detail: The US president posted on Truth Social that the task force is fully in effect and, together with what he called history's greatest naval blockade, very little goods get into or out of Iran.

squawks.headline: Drone attack halts production at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field in the Kurdistan region
squawks.detail: Two security sources said output stopped on Sunday at the field, one of the largest in the Kurdistan region. An engineer at the site reported a fire at a gas storage facility.

squawks.headline: Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to let its oil exports pass through Hormuz via a lane near Oman
squawks.detail: Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that Iraqi oil exports would use a shipping lane near Oman under the arrangement with Washington.

squawks.headline: US Treasury asks Iraq to close all but two of its border crossings with Iran, Iraqi foreign minister says
squawks.detail: Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that the request forms part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran.

squawks.headline: Iranian state broadcaster reports two blasts heard near Suza on Qeshm Island, with no casualties reported
squawks.detail: Iran's state broadcaster cited an informed source on two explosions near the Suza area of Qeshm Island and said there were no casualty reports. Earlier, Tasnim had reported two missiles striking the island without official confirmation.

squawks.headline: Early Tasnim reports say two missiles struck Iran's Qeshm Island; no official confirmation yet
squawks.detail: Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency says initial reports point to two missiles hitting Qeshm Island, but officials have not confirmed this. The reports do not say who fired the missiles, and no market reaction has been reported.

squawks.headline: US consumer credit rises $27.84bn in September, well above the $13.8bn forecast
squawks.detail: US consumer credit grew by $27.84bn in September, against a forecast of $13.8bn and up from $8.28bn the month before.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is in talks with Iran and has been for some time
squawks.detail: President Trump told reporters that Washington is talking to Tehran. No details of the talks or any market reaction were reported.

squawks.headline: Oil traders reportedly in talks with US over using sanctioned tankers to bring down freight costs and oil prices
squawks.detail: A market news account reported that oil traders are discussing with the US the use of tankers under sanctions, with the aim of easing freight rates and oil prices. Separately, Brent crude futures settled 3 cents higher at $98.32 a barrel.

squawks.headline: US Treasury announces new sanctions related to Iran
squawks.detail: The US Treasury Department announced a new round of Iran-related sanctions on Friday. No details or market reaction were given in the initial report.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says intelligence points to planned Russian strikes on energy sites, Dnipro bridges and infrastructure
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said intelligence shows Russian forces are preparing new strikes on energy targets, bridges over the Dnipro river and other infrastructure. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: USTR Greer says China must carry out its agricultural and rare earths commitments
squawks.detail: US Trade Representative Greer said China needs to implement its pledges on agriculture and rare earths. This follows earlier US calls for Beijing to meet the terms of the Busan trade truce.

squawks.headline: Italy has not yet backed either the Spanish or the Dutch candidate to succeed Lagarde as ECB president
squawks.detail: Officials in Italian Prime Minister Meloni's office said on Friday that Rome has not yet chosen between the two candidates to replace Christine Lagarde as ECB president, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says he does not foresee a US recession
squawks.detail: The chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers said on 6 November that he does not expect a recession at all. He spoke after the October US jobs report.

squawks.headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says the next US CPI print will show what the Fed does next
squawks.detail: The chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers said the next US consumer price data would need to be seen before judging the Fed's next move. He made the remarks after the October jobs report.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says policy may be anywhere from slightly restrictive to neutral and services inflation is not easing as expected
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said on Friday that US rates could sit between slightly restrictive and neutral. She added that services inflation is not falling in the way policymakers would expect.

squawks.headline: Canadian dollar falls to a near three-week low against the US dollar after an unexpected drop in October jobs
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the Canadian dollar weakened on Friday after data showed the economy lost jobs for a third month in a row. The data cooled expectations of Bank of Canada rate hikes.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says the recent painful market volatility amounts to the kind of rebalancing policymakers would want
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that, looking past the painful volatility, the adjustment is the sort of rebalancing the Fed would hope to see.

squawks.headline: Canada's PM Carney says Ottawa is in talks with China on next steps for trade
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is talking to China about the next steps in developing trade between the two countries.

squawks.headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says he does not expect the Fed to treat the October jobs report as inflationary
squawks.detail: Council of Economic Advisers Chair Phelan commented on the October US payrolls report on Friday.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says further policy tightening will be needed and the solid job market gives room to finish the inflation fight
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said she wants to be more confident on inflation and that holding at the last meeting was right given uncertainty. She called the AI repricing orderly so far, said it could ease her view slightly if it signals slower demand growth, and said businesses are cautiously optimistic.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly calls the October jobs report good news for US workers and says wage growth is not booming
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly commented on the October payrolls report in remarks reported via CNBC. She described the report as positive for American workers and said wage growth is not running hot.

squawks.headline: Canada's PM Carney says Ottawa will keep working with the US towards a trade deal that suits Canada
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Friday that Canada would carry on talks with the United States aimed at a trade agreement that works for Canada. He gave no timetable or new terms.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine keeps striking Russia's oil sector in response to Russian attacks on energy sites
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv is continuing to target Russian oil sector facilities, in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says he and USTR Greer held talks with China's Vice Premier He Lifeng on economic ties
squawks.detail: Bessent said that during the call with He Lifeng, he and Greer pressed China to honour its commitments under the Busan arrangement in full and without delay.

squawks.headline: Putin and Russia's Security Council discuss the upcoming Ukraine talks
squawks.detail: Reports say President Putin discussed the forthcoming Ukraine negotiations with Russia's Security Council. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Qatar's prime minister says the US and Iran will not be able to reach a perfect deal
squawks.detail: Qatar's prime minister commented on the US-Iran negotiations as mediators' proposals are under review in Tehran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US tells China to meet the terms of the Busan trade truce immediately; officials say Beijing has met only two-thirds of rare earth pledges
squawks.detail: US officials say China has not raised rare earth supply and has delivered on only two-thirds of its rare earth commitments. The FT reports that Washington has warned Beijing it must comply with the Busan trade truce immediately.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the aim is to hold underlying inflation at 2% and that the Bank has made no formal commitment on its communication
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan Governor said that with underlying inflation now at 2%, the goal is to keep it at that level, and that the Bank is discussing how it communicates but has no formal commitment yet. He also reported a sharp rise in cyber attacks in Japan over the past one to two months.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the Bank watches other central banks closely, calls AI a positive demand shock and flags cyber risks to financial stability
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan Governor said other central banks' actions affect asset prices including exchange rates and interest rates, and that AI has been a positive demand shock for Japan, which may benefit from AI replacing labour given significant labour shortages. On financial stability, he named cyber risks as a concern and said the Bank has been identifying vulnerable areas, including some small banks and small firms with weak protection.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda puts Japanese consumer inflation near 3%, sees upside risks and says unconventional tools could return after big shocks
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said consumer prices are around 3% and expected to rise further into early next year as energy-related costs feed through, with underlying inflation likely to stay around 2% but facing upside risks. He said unconventional tools have had some positive effects but are not perfect substitutes for rate cuts from positive levels, and the Bank may have to use them again in a severe shock, in a way that limits the side effects.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says 2% inflation is not yet a social norm in Japan and the Bank has heard no major complaints about higher rates
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said wages are growing at a pace consistent with 2% inflation but it is not yet known whether that balance can last a long time. He added that real rates have not risen by as much, and that much work remains on inflation.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation in Japan has hit 2% for the first time in decades and normalisation targets price stability
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan governor said policy normalisation is aimed at price stability. He added that once it is achieved, nominal variables will do less to get in the way of resource allocation.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says the BoJ's policy normalisation has gone impressively smoothly
squawks.detail: The IMF Managing Director praised how smoothly the Bank of Japan has normalised its monetary policy.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda expects domestic investment in Japan to rise but says the scale is highly uncertain
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said he expects domestic investment in Japan to increase, though how far it will rise is very uncertain. The remarks came during the same appearance as his earlier comments on corporate saving and the current account.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japanese firms spent years repaying debt after the bubble burst, and corporate saving stayed high afterwards
squawks.detail: In further remarks, the Bank of Japan Governor said Japan's experience shows why corporate adjustment matters. He said firms cut investment and repaired their balance sheets after the bubble collapsed, and that overseas investment grew in importance once that process was largely over.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japan's 1990s demographic decline cut expected returns on domestic capital at home
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said Japan's demographic decline in the 1990s held down the expected return on domestic capital. He added that a severe scarcity has only become a reality in recent years.

squawks.headline: Eurogroup names Spain's de Cos and the Netherlands' Knot as the only two candidates for ECB president
squawks.detail: The Eurogroup says former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot are the two candidates to become the next ECB president. No other candidates have been put forward.

squawks.headline: French finance minister says the diesel sale is part of a plan to release 10 million barrels from stocks
squawks.detail: France's finance minister says the diesel sold so far from strategic reserves belongs to a wider 10 million barrel stock release plan. Earlier, the energy ministry put the amount of diesel sold at 3.6 million barrels.

squawks.headline: Proposals to Iran cover its highly enriched uranium stockpile and offer major US sanctions relief, Times of Israel reports
squawks.detail: According to a diplomat familiar with the talks, the proposals do not go as far as fully dismantling Iran's nuclear programme. They do deal with Tehran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium and would give Iran significant sanctions relief from the US, the Times of Israel reports.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japan's current account has shifted sharply and is now driven by income flows
squawks.detail: In a speech, the Bank of Japan Governor described a marked shift in Japan's current account, which he said is now driven by income flows. He did not comment on the economic or policy outlook.

squawks.headline: Iranian negotiators review proposals to limit Tehran's nuclear programme, Times of Israel reports
squawks.detail: The Times of Israel, citing a US official and a diplomat, reported that Iranian negotiators are reviewing proposals to curb the nuclear programme, an issue Tehran had long refused to discuss.

squawks.headline: France has sold 3.6 million barrels of diesel from its strategic reserves so far, energy ministry says
squawks.detail: The French energy ministry said 3.6 million barrels of diesel have been released from the country's strategic reserves to date.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva flags concern over large, rising global imbalances and expects AI-related market volatility to persist
squawks.detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said widening global imbalances have often come with fragile growth and have sometimes preceded financial crises. She also said market volatility linked to AI is likely to continue.

squawks.headline: IMF's Georgieva says central banks must look through uncertainty and weigh any slowdown in AI-driven growth in the inflation fight
squawks.detail: The IMF Managing Director said the AI investment boom and high valuations are affecting markets worldwide. She added that if the growth boost from AI slowed, central banks would need to factor that in as they decide their next steps against inflation.

squawks.headline: Polish foreign minister Sikorski says no deal to end the war can be reached without Ukraine and Europe
squawks.detail: Poland's foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski said on Friday that an agreement on the war in Ukraine cannot be made over the heads of Ukraine and Europe. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: EU's Kallas says Putin has no veto over European security and Ukraine must become part of its security architecture
squawks.detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also said Russian sabotage across Europe must stop. She made the remarks on Friday as talks continue over a possible Ukraine settlement.

squawks.headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says the EU must be part of any Ukraine peace deal
squawks.detail: The EU's foreign policy chief said the EU would need to be involved in any peace agreement on Ukraine. Separately, Poland's foreign minister said no settlement can be imposed on Ukraine unless it agrees and takes part.

squawks.headline: European officials fear a US security deal with Russia could undermine NATO, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that European officials are concerned Washington could reach a security agreement with Moscow that weakens NATO and restores a Russian sphere of influence.

squawks.headline: Polish foreign minister says a ceasefire must come before Ukraine peace talks can begin
squawks.detail: Poland's foreign minister set a ceasefire as a precondition for starting Ukraine peace talks. The US has said it will host US-Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

squawks.headline: CDS on US hyperscalers and chipmakers widen to levels implying heavy ratings downgrades as the AI debt sell-off spreads
squawks.detail: IFR reports that a sharp sell-off in debt has pushed credit default swaps on US hyperscalers and chipmakers to levels consistent with large ratings downgrades, with Oracle and SpaceX swaps trading well into junk territory. Reuters separately reports that traders' focus is shifting from inflation to growth as the tech rout deepens, raising questions over room for further central bank rate hikes.

squawks.headline: Canada's Ivey PMI edges up to 58.3 in October from 58.2
squawks.detail: Canada's Ivey purchasing managers' index came in at 58.3 for October, against 58.2 the previous month. No consensus forecast was given.

squawks.headline: US UMich sentiment rises to 51 in preliminary reading against a 48 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations ease to 4.3%
squawks.detail: The University of Michigan preliminary sentiment index came in at 51 against a 48 forecast and 48.0 previously; current conditions were 51 (forecast 47, previous 46.7) and expectations 50.9 (forecast 49, previous 48.8). One-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7% (forecast 4.6%), and five-year expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5% (forecast 3.5%).

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says clear Fed communication helps policy pass through to the economy more smoothly
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said that good communication from the Fed leads to smoother transmission of monetary policy. The remark was part of his comments on Friday.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says inflation is falling and he sees no policy change that needs planning
squawks.detail: The National Economic Council's Hassett said the data show strong growth and slowing inflation, that the administration's policies are working, and that the job market is firing on all cylinders.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says excess US inflation comes from both supply and demand; expects AI to lift productivity sharply
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the data centre build-out is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says Trump will decide on Fed Governor Cook after reading the report
squawks.detail: Senior White House adviser Hassett also said headline inflation is being driven by energy and Iran, and that he sees no need to plan a policy change.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem blames excess US inflation on energy shocks and the AI build-out; says consumption and investment are growing fast
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation must come back to 2% in a timely way. He said data-centre construction is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says public concern about current inflation persists but expectations remain anchored
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said people are still worried about inflation at its present level. He also said inflation expectations remain anchored.

squawks.headline: Iranian source says Tehran is responding positively to the latest proposal from mediators
squawks.detail: An Iranian source told Al Arabiya that Tehran is responding positively to the newest proposal put forward by mediators in the US-Iran talks. Separately, a senior Iranian security official repeated that Tehran wants concrete US action before a new phase of diplomacy.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett points to three months of strong US job growth and says inflation should be slowing
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said he was looking at the last three months of very strong job growth and, when asked about the Fed, said inflation should be slowing. He also said an AI bubble is a fair concern, but the US economy could still be very strong even if data centre building slows.

squawks.headline: ECB considers reviewing bank lending to data centres
squawks.detail: The ECB is weighing a review of bank loans to data centres, according to a market news post on Friday afternoon. No timing or scope was given.
